verses.1:1: In the second year of the reign of Artaxerxes the great king, on the first day of Nisan, Mordecai the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin, saw a dream—a Jewish man dwelling in the city of Susa, a great man, serving in the court of the king. Now he was from the captivity which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away captive from Jerusalem with Jeconiah the king of Judea. And this was his dream: Behold, cries and uproar, thunderings and earthquake, tumult upon the earth. And behold, two great dragons came forth, both ready to wrestle; and their cry was great, and at their cry every nation made ready for war, to fight against a nation of the righteous. And behold, a day of darkness and gloom, tribulation and anguish, affliction and great tumult upon the earth; and all the righteous nation was troubled, fearing their own evils, and they prepared to perish; and they cried out to God. And from their cry there came, as it were from a small spring, a great river, abundant water; light and the sun rose, and the lowly were exalted and devoured the glorious. And when Mordecai awoke, having seen this dream and what God had purposed to do, he kept it in his heart, and in every way he desired to understand it until the night. And Mordecai rested in the court with Gabatha and Tharra, the two eunuchs of the king who guarded the court, and he heard their reasonings and searched out their designs, and learned that they were preparing to lay hands on Artaxerxes the king. And he informed the king concerning them; and the king examined the two eunuchs, and when they confessed, they were led away. And the king wrote these matters for a memorial, and Mordecai also wrote concerning these matters; and the king commanded Mordecai to serve in the court, and gave him gifts for these things. Now Haman the son of Hammedatha, a Bougaean, was honored before the king, and he sought to harm Mordecai and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king. And it came to pass after these things, in the days of Artaxerxes—this is the Artaxerxes who ruled from India over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces.
verses.1:2: In those very days, when King Artaxerxes was enthroned in the city of Susa,
verses.1:3: in the third year of his reign, he made a banquet for his friends and for the other nations, and for the nobles of the Persians and Medes, and for the rulers of the satraps.
verses.1:4: And after these things, after showing them the riches of his kingdom and the glory of the gladness of his riches for one hundred and eighty days,
verses.1:5: when the days of the marriage feast were fulfilled, the king made a drinking feast for the nations found in the city for six days in the court of the king's house,
verses.1:6: adorned with fine linen and cotton hangings stretched upon cords of fine linen and purple, upon blocks of gold and silver, upon pillars of Parian marble and stone; couches of gold and silver were upon a pavement of emerald stone, and mother-of-pearl, and Parian marble, and transparent coverings variously embroidered with flowers, with roses strewn all around;
verses.1:7: cups of gold and silver, and a small carbuncle goblet set forth, worth thirty thousand talents; abundant and sweet wine, such as the king himself drank.
verses.1:8: Now this drinking feast was not according to an established law; rather, the king so desired, and he commanded the stewards to do his will and the will of the men.
verses.1:9: And Queen Astin also made a drinking feast for the women in the royal palace where King Artaxerxes was.
verses.1:10: And on the seventh day, when the king had become merry, he spoke to Aman, Mazan, Tharra, Boraze, Zatholtha, Abataza, and Tharaba, the seven eunuchs who served King Artaxerxes,
verses.1:11: to bring the queen in to him, that she might reign as queen, and to place the diadem upon her, and to display her to the rulers and her beauty to the nations, for she was fair.
verses.1:12: But Queen Astin would not obey him to come with the eunuchs; and the king was grieved and grew angry,
verses.1:13: and he said to his friends, "In this manner Astin has spoken; therefore establish law and judgment concerning this."
verses.1:14: Then Arcesaeus, Sarsathaeus, and Malesear, the rulers of the Persians and Medes who were near the king, who sat first beside the king, came to him,
verses.1:15: and declared to him according to the laws what ought to be done to Queen Astin, because she had not done the things commanded by the king through the eunuchs.
verses.1:16: And Muchaeus said to the king and the rulers, "Queen Astin has wronged not the king alone, but also all the rulers and leaders of the king."
verses.1:17: For indeed he recounted to them the words of the queen, and how she had contradicted the king. "Therefore, just as she contradicted King Artaxerxes,
verses.1:18: so today the other noble ladies of the rulers of the Persians and Medes, having heard the things spoken by her to the king, will likewise dare to dishonor their own husbands.
verses.1:19: If therefore it pleases the king, let him issue a royal decree, and let it be written according to the laws of the Medes and Persians, and let him not do otherwise, nor let the queen come in before him any more, and let the king give her royal estate to a woman better than she.
verses.1:20: And let the law which the king makes be heard throughout his kingdom; and thus all women will bestow honor upon their own husbands, from poor to rich."
verses.1:21: And the word pleased the king and the rulers; and the king did just as Muchaeus had spoken,
verses.1:22: and he sent into all the kingdom, to every province according to its language, that there might be fear of them in their own houses.
verses.2:1: And after these things the king ceased from his wrath, and no longer remembered Astin, recalling what she had spoken and how he had condemned her.
verses.2:2: Then the servants of the king said, "Let uncorrupted maidens, fair in appearance, be sought for the king;
verses.2:3: and let the king appoint local governors in all the provinces of his kingdom, and let them select virgin maidens, fair in appearance, to be brought to the city of Susa into the women's quarters; and let them be delivered to the king's eunuch, the keeper of the women, and let ointments and all other care be given to them;
verses.2:4: and the woman who pleases the king shall reign as queen instead of Astin." And the counsel pleased the king, and he did so.
verses.2:5: Now there was a Jewish man in the city of Susa, and his name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin,
verses.2:6: who had been carried away captive from Jerusalem, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive.
verses.2:7: And he had a foster child, the daughter of Amminadab, his father's brother, and her name was Esther; and when her parents died, he brought her up for himself as a wife; and the maiden was fair in appearance.
verses.2:8: And when the decree of the king was heard, many maidens were gathered to the city of Susa under the hand of Gai, and Esther was brought to Gai, the keeper of the women.
verses.2:9: And the maiden pleased him, and she found favor before him; and he hastened to give her the ointments and her portion, and the seven maidens appointed for her from the royal house, and he treated her and her attendants well in the women's quarters.
verses.2:10: And Esther did not reveal her lineage nor her homeland, for Mordecai had commanded her not to declare it.
verses.2:11: And every day Mordecai walked about by the court of the women, watching to see what would happen to Esther.
verses.2:12: Now this was the appointed time for a maiden to go in to the king, when she had completed twelve months; for thus the days of their care were fulfilled: six months anointing themselves with oil of myrrh, and six months with spices and with the ointments of women.
verses.2:13: And then she would go in to the king; and to whomever she named, he would deliver her to go in with him from the women's quarters to the royal palace.
verses.2:14: In the evening she would go in, and toward morning she would return to the second women's quarters, where Gai the king's eunuch, the keeper of the women, was; and she would not go in to the king again unless she was called by name.
verses.2:15: Now when the time was fulfilled for Esther, the daughter of Amminadab the brother of Mordecai's father, to go in to the king, she neglected nothing of the things which the eunuch, the keeper of the women, commanded; for Esther found favor with all who looked upon her.
verses.2:16: So Esther went in to King Artaxerxes in the twelfth month, which is Adar, in the seventh year of his reign.
verses.2:17: And the king loved Esther, and she found favor above all the virgins, and he placed the queenly diadem upon her.
verses.2:18: And the king made a drinking feast for all his friends and his forces for seven days, and he exalted the wedding of Esther, and granted a remission to those under his kingdom.
verses.2:19: Meanwhile, Mordecai was serving in the court.
verses.2:20: And Esther did not reveal her homeland; for so Mordecai had commanded her, to fear God and to keep His commandments, just as when she was with him; and Esther did not change her way of life.
verses.2:21: And the two eunuchs of the king, the chief bodyguards, were grieved because Mordecai had been promoted, and they sought to kill King Artaxerxes.
verses.2:22: And the matter was made known to Mordecai, and he informed Esther, and she disclosed the details of the plot to the king.
verses.2:23: Then the king examined the two eunuchs and hanged them; and the king commanded that a memorial be entered in the royal library concerning the goodwill of Mordecai in commendation of him.
verses.3:1: Now after these things King Artaxerxes glorified Haman the son of Hammedatha, a Bougaean, and exalted him, and he held the first seat among all his friends.
verses.3:2: And all who were in the court bowed down to him, for so the king had commanded to be done; but Mordecai would not bow down to him.
verses.3:3: And those who were in the king's court spoke to Mordecai, "Mordecai, why do you disregard the things spoken by the king?"
verses.3:4: Day by day they spoke to him, and he did not listen to them; so they reported to Haman that Mordecai was opposing the words of the king; and Mordecai had declared to them that he was a Jew.
verses.3:5: And when Haman perceived that Mordecai did not bow down to him, he was filled with great wrath,
verses.3:6: and he purposed to destroy all the Jews who were under the kingdom of Artaxerxes.
verses.3:7: And he made a decree in the twelfth year of the reign of Artaxerxes, and cast lots day by day and month by month, to destroy in one day the race of Mordecai; and the lot fell on the fourteenth day of the month which is Adar.
verses.3:8: And he spoke to King Artaxerxes, saying, "There is a nation scattered among the nations in all your kingdom, and their laws are different from all the nations, and they disregard the laws of the king, and it is not profitable for the king to leave them alone.
verses.3:9: If it pleases the king, let him decree to destroy them, and I will pay into the treasury of the king ten thousand talents of silver."
verses.3:10: Then the king took off his signet ring and gave it into the hand of Haman, to seal what was written against the Jews.
verses.3:11: And the king said to Haman, "Keep the silver, and deal with the nation as you wish."
verses.3:12: So the scribes of the king were summoned on the thirteenth day of the first month, and they wrote as Haman commanded to the generals and to the rulers in every province from India to Ethiopia, to the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces, and to the rulers of the nations according to their own language, in the name of King Artaxerxes.
verses.3:13: And it was sent by couriers into the kingdom of Artaxerxes, to destroy the race of the Jews in one day of the twelfth month, which is Adar, and to plunder their possessions. Now this is the copy of the letter: "The Great King Artaxerxes writes these things to the rulers of the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces from India to Ethiopia, and to the governors subject to him: Having ruled over many nations and gained dominion over the whole inhabited world, I purposed—not being lifted up by the boldness of authority, but always conducting affairs with forbearance and gentleness—to establish the lives of my subjects continually calm and untroubled, and, making the kingdom peaceable and safe for travel to its utmost borders, to restore the peace longed for by all mankind. Now when I inquired of my counselors how this might be brought to fulfillment, Haman, who excels among us in soundness of mind, and has been proven steadfast in unswerving goodwill and firm loyalty, and has attained the second place of honor in the kingdom, pointed out to us that among all the tribes throughout the inhabited world there is mingled a certain hostile people, opposed in their laws to every nation, and continually disregarding the commands of kings, so that the united governance blamelessly directed by us cannot be established. Having therefore understood that this nation alone stands continually in opposition to all mankind, turning aside to a strange manner of life under alien laws, and being ill-disposed toward our affairs, committing the worst evils, so that the kingdom cannot attain stability; we have therefore commanded that those indicated to you in the letters written by Haman, who is appointed over our affairs and is our second father, shall all, together with wives and children, be utterly destroyed root and branch by the swords of their enemies, without any pity or sparing, on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar, of the present year, so that those who both of old and now are hostile, having gone down violently in one day into Hades, may for the time to come leave our affairs completely stable and untroubled to the end."
verses.3:14: And copies of the letters were posted in every province; and it was commanded to all the nations to be ready for this day.
verses.3:15: And the matter was hastened also in Susa; and the king and Haman drank heavily together, while the city was thrown into confusion.
verses.4:1: Now Mordecai, learning of what was being done, tore his garments, put on sackcloth, and sprinkled ashes upon himself; and rushing out through the broad square of the city, he cried out with a loud voice, "A nation that has done no wrong is being swept away!"
verses.4:2: And he came as far as the king's gate and stood there, for it was not lawful for him to enter the courtyard wearing sackcloth and ashes.
verses.4:3: And in every province where the letters were posted, there was outcry, wailing, and great mourning among the Jews; they spread sackcloth and ashes for themselves.
verses.4:4: And the maidservants and the eunuchs of the queen came in and told her; and she was deeply troubled upon hearing what had happened, and sent to clothe Mordecai and take away his sackcloth, but he would not consent.
verses.4:5: Then Esther summoned Achrathaeus her eunuch, who stood in attendance upon her, and sent him to learn the exact truth for her from Mordecai.
verses.4:7: And Mordecai showed him what had happened and the promise of ten thousand talents that Haman had promised the king for the treasury in order to destroy the Jews.
verses.4:8: He also gave him the copy posted in Susa for their destruction, to show to Esther, and told him to charge her to go in, plead with the king, and petition him on behalf of the people: "Remember the days of your lowliness, how you were reared by my hand; for Haman, who holds second place to the king, has spoken against us for death. Call upon the Lord, and speak to the king for us, and deliver us from death."
verses.4:9: So Achrathaeus went in and spoke all these words to her.
verses.4:10: Then Esther said to Achrathaeus, "Go to Mordecai and say,
verses.4:11: 'All the nations of the kingdom know that for any man or woman who goes in to the king into the inner courtyard unsummoned, there is no deliverance—only the one to whom the king extends the golden scepter shall be saved; and I myself have not been summoned to go in to the king these thirty days.'"
verses.4:12: And Achrathaeus reported to Mordecai all the words of Esther.
verses.4:13: And Mordecai said to Achrathaeus, "Go and say to her, 'Esther, do not say to yourself that you alone will be saved in the kingdom above all the Jews;
verses.4:14: for if you fail to heed at this time, help and protection will come to the Jews from another quarter, while you and the house of your father shall perish. And who knows whether you became queen for this very time?'"
verses.4:15: Then Esther sent the one who had come to her back to Mordecai, saying,
verses.4:16: "Go, assemble the Jews who are in Susa, and fast on my behalf; neither eat nor drink for three days, night and day, and I and my maidservants will likewise abstain from food. Then I will go in to the king contrary to the law, even if it be that I must perish."
verses.4:17: So Mordecai went and did all that Esther had commanded him. And he prayed to the Lord, calling to remembrance all the works of the Lord, and said, "O Lord, Lord, King ruling over all things, for all things are in Your power, and there is no one who can oppose You when You will to save Israel; for You made heaven and earth and every wondrous thing beneath heaven, and You are Lord of all, and there is no one who shall withstand You, the Lord. You know all things; You know, O Lord, that it was not in insolence, nor in pride, nor in love of glory that I did this—refusing to bow down before the arrogant Haman; for I would gladly have kissed the soles of his feet for the salvation of Israel. Rather, I did this so that I might not set the glory of a man above the glory of God; and I will not bow down to anyone except You, my Lord, nor will I do these things in pride. And now, O Lord God, the King, the God of Abraham, spare Your people; for they look upon us for destruction, and they have desired to destroy Your inheritance from the beginning. Do not overlook Your portion, which You redeemed for Yourself out of the land of Egypt. Hear my supplication and be merciful to Your allotted heritage, and turn our mourning into feasting, that living we may sing praise to Your name, O Lord; and do not blot out the mouth of those who praise You." And all Israel cried out with all their might, because their death was before their eyes. And Esther the queen fled for refuge to the Lord, seized with the agony of death; and taking off the garments of her splendor, she put on garments of distress and mourning, and instead of exquisite perfumes she filled her head with ashes and dung; and she humbled her body exceedingly, and every place of her joyful adornment she covered with her tangled hair. And she prayed to the Lord God of Israel and said, "My Lord, our King, You are the only One; help me, alone as I am and having no helper except You, for my peril is in my hand. From my birth I have heard in the tribe of my father's house that You, O Lord, took Israel out of all the nations, and our fathers out of all their ancestors, for an everlasting inheritance, and that You did for them all that You spoke. And now we have sinned before You, and You have delivered us into the hands of our enemies because we gave glory to their gods. Righteous are You, O Lord! Yet now they are not satisfied with the bitterness of our bondage, but they have set their hands to abolish the decree of Your mouth, and to blot out Your inheritance, and to shut the mouth of those who praise You, and to quench the glory of Your house and Your altar, and to open the mouth of the nations in praise of worthless things, and that a king of flesh should be marveled at forever. Do not surrender Your scepter, O Lord, to those who do not exist, and do not let them mock at our downfall; but turn their counsel back upon themselves, and make a public example of the one who began this against us. Remember, O Lord; make Yourself known in the time of our affliction, and give me courage, O King of the gods and Sovereign over every dominion. Put well-ordered speech into my mouth before the lion, and turn his heart to hatred of the one who makes war against us, to the utter ruin of him and of those who are of one mind with him. But deliver us by Your hand, and help me, alone as I am and having no one except You, O Lord. You have knowledge of all things, and You know that I have hated the glory of the lawless, and I abhor the bed of the uncircumcised and of every foreigner. You know my necessity—that I abhor the emblem of my high station which is upon my head on the days of my public appearance; I abhor it like a menstrual cloth, and I do not wear it on the days of my quietness. And Your handmaid has not eaten at Haman's table, nor have I honored the king's banquet, nor have I drunk the wine of drink offerings. And Your handmaid has not rejoiced from the day of my change of fortune until now, except in You, O Lord, the God of Abraham. O God, mighty over all, hear the voice of those in despair, and deliver us out of the hand of evildoers, and deliver me from my fear."
verses.5:1: Now it came to pass on the third day, when she ceased praying, that she took off the garments of worship and arrayed herself in her splendor. And having become resplendent, after calling upon God, the Overseer of all and Savior, she took with her the two maidservants; upon the one she leaned delicately, while the other followed behind, lifting up her robe. And she was radiant in the prime of her beauty, and her countenance was cheerful and lovely, yet her heart was constricted with fear. Having passed through all the doors, she stood before the king; and he was seated upon his royal throne, clothed in all the array of his majesty, wholly adorned with gold and precious stones, and he was exceedingly terrifying. Lifting up his countenance, blazing with splendor, he looked at her in the fierceness of wrath; and the queen fell down, her color changed as she fainted, and she sank down upon the head of the maidservant who went before her. Then God changed the spirit of the king into gentleness, and in anxiety he sprang up from his throne and took her into his arms until she recovered, and he comforted her with words of peace and said to her, "What is it, Esther? I am your brother. Take courage; you shall not die, for our decree is a general one. Come near."
verses.5:2: And lifting up the golden scepter, he laid it upon her neck, embraced her, and said, "Speak to me." And she said to him, "I saw you, my lord, like an angel of God, and my heart was troubled in fear of your glory; for you are wondrous, my lord, and your countenance is full of grace." Yet as she was speaking, she fell down from faintness; and the king was distressed, and all his attendants comforted her.
verses.5:3: Then the king said, "What do you wish, Esther, and what is your petition? Even up to half of my kingdom, it shall be yours."
verses.5:4: And Esther said, "Today is a special day for me; if therefore it pleases the king, let both him and Haman come to the banquet that I will prepare today."
verses.5:5: And the king said, "Hasten Haman, that we may carry out the word of Esther." So both of them came to the banquet of which Esther had spoken.
verses.5:6: Now during the drinking, the king said to Esther, "What is it, Queen Esther? Whatever you request shall be granted."
verses.5:7: And she said, "My request and my petition:
verses.5:8: if I have found favor before the king, let the king and Haman come again tomorrow to the banquet that I will prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do the same."
verses.5:9: So Haman went out from the king overjoyed and glad; yet when Haman saw Mordecai the Jew in the courtyard, he became exceedingly angry.
verses.5:10: And entering his own house, he called together his friends and Zosara his wife,
verses.5:11: and he displayed to them his wealth and the glory with which the king had invested him, and how he had appointed him to hold first place and to lead the kingdom.
verses.5:12: And Haman said, "The queen has invited no one with the king to the banquet except me; and for tomorrow also I am invited.
verses.5:13: Yet these things do not please me whenever I see Mordecai the Jew in the courtyard."
verses.5:14: Then Zosara his wife and his friends said to him, "Let a beam of fifty cubits be hewn for you, and at dawn speak to the king, and let Mordecai be hanged upon the beam; then go in to the banquet with the king and rejoice." And the saying pleased Haman, and the beam was made ready.
verses.6:1: Now the Lord took sleep away from the king that night, and he told his tutor to bring in the memorial writings of the days to read to him.
verses.6:2: And he found the records written concerning Mordecai, how he had reported to the king concerning the two eunuchs of the king, while they were standing guard and sought to lay hands on Artaxerxes.
verses.6:3: Then the king said, "What honor or favor have we done for Mordecai?" And the servants of the king said, "You have done nothing for him."
verses.6:4: Now while the king was inquiring concerning the loyalty of Mordecai, behold, Haman was in the courtyard. And the king said, "Who is in the courtyard?" For Haman had entered to tell the king to hang Mordecai upon the beam that he had prepared.
verses.6:5: And the servants of the king said, "Behold, Haman is standing in the courtyard." And the king said, "Call him."
verses.6:6: And the king said to Haman, "What shall I do for the man whom I wish to honor?" Now Haman said within himself, "Whom does the king wish to honor except me?"
verses.6:7: And he said to the king, "For the man whom the king wishes to honor,
verses.6:8: let the servants of the king bring a fine linen robe that the king wears, and a horse upon which the king rides,
verses.6:9: and let him give them to one of the king's illustrious friends, and let him array the man whom the king loves, and mount him upon the horse, and proclaim through the broad square of the city, saying, 'So shall it be for every man whom the king honors.'"
verses.6:10: Then the king said to Haman, "You have spoken well; do thus for Mordecai the Jew, who serves in the courtyard, and do not let a single word fail of what you have spoken."
verses.6:11: So Haman took the robe and the horse, arrayed Mordecai, mounted him upon the horse, and passed through the broad square of the city, proclaiming and saying, "So shall it be for every man whom the king wishes to honor."
verses.6:12: Then Mordecai returned to the courtyard, while Haman went back to his own house, grieving with his head covered.
verses.6:13: And Haman recounted what had befallen him to Zosara his wife and to his friends. And his friends and his wife said to him, "If Mordecai is of the race of the Jews, you have begun to be humbled before him—you shall surely fall! You will by no means be able to defend yourself against him, because the living God is with him."
verses.6:14: While they were still speaking, the eunuchs arrived, hurrying Haman to the wine banquet that Esther had prepared.
verses.7:1: Now the king and Haman went in to drink with the queen.
verses.7:2: And on the second day, at the drinking feast, the king said to Esther, "What is it, Queen Esther, and what is your petition, and what is your request? Let it be yours, even to half of my kingdom."
verses.7:3: And answering, she said, "If I have found favor before the king, let my life be given at my petition, and my word at my request.
verses.7:4: For we have been sold, both I and my people, to destruction and plunder and bondage, we and our children to be menservants and maidservants, and I paid no heed; for the slanderer is not worthy of the king's court."
verses.7:5: Then the king said, "Who is this man who has dared to do this thing?"
verses.7:6: And Esther said, "A man who is an enemy—this wicked Haman!" And Haman was dismayed before the king and the queen.
verses.7:7: Now the king arose from the banquet into the garden; but Haman pleaded with the queen, for he saw himself in dire straits.
verses.7:8: And the king returned from the garden, and Haman had fallen upon the couch, pleading with the queen. Then the king said, "Will you even assault my wife in my house?" And when Haman heard this, he was confounded in his countenance.
verses.7:9: Then Bugathan, one of the eunuchs, said to the king, "Behold, Haman has also prepared a gallows for Mordecai, who spoke concerning the king, and a gallows fifty cubits high stands erected at Haman's house." And the king said, "Let him be crucified upon it."
verses.7:10: So Haman was hanged upon the gallows that had been prepared for Mordecai. And then the king ceased from his wrath.
verses.8:1: And on that same day King Artaxerxes bestowed upon Esther all that belonged to Haman the slanderer, and Mordecai was summoned by the king; for Esther had disclosed that he was related to her.
verses.8:2: And the king took the signet ring that he had taken away from Haman and gave it to Mordecai; and Esther appointed Mordecai over all that belonged to Haman.
verses.8:3: And she spoke yet again to the king, and fell down at his feet, and pleaded with him to remove the wickedness of Haman and all that he had done to the Jews.
verses.8:4: Then the king extended the golden scepter to Esther; so Esther arose to stand before the king.
verses.8:5: And Esther said, "If it pleases you and I have found favor, let an order be sent to recall the letters dispatched by Haman, which were written that the Jews who are in your kingdom should perish.
verses.8:6: For how shall I be able to behold the affliction of my people, and how shall I be able to be saved in the destruction of my homeland?"
verses.8:7: Then the king said to Esther, "If I have given and graciously bestowed upon you all the possessions of Haman, and have hanged him upon a gallows because he laid his hands upon the Jews, what more do you seek?
verses.8:8: Write also yourselves in my name as seems good to you, and seal it with my signet ring; for all things that are written at the king's command and sealed with my signet ring cannot be contradicted."
verses.8:9: Then the scribes were summoned in the first month, which is Nisa, on the twenty-third day of that same year; and there was written to the Jews all that he commanded the stewards and the rulers of the satraps from India to Ethiopia, across one hundred and twenty-seven satrapies, province by province, according to their own language.
verses.8:10: And it was written by the king and sealed with his signet ring, and they sent out the letters by couriers,
verses.8:11: in which he commanded them to observe their own laws in every city, and to defend themselves, and to deal with their adversaries and their opponents as they wished,
verses.8:12: on one day throughout all the kingdom of Artaxerxes, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is Adar. Now the copy of the letter is what is written below: "The great King Artaxerxes, to the rulers of the provinces in the one hundred and twenty-seven satrapies from India to Ethiopia, and to those loyal to our interests, greetings. Many who are more frequently honored by the exceedingly great goodness of their benefactors have become arrogant, and not only do they seek to harm our subjects, but being unable to bear their abundance, they even undertake to scheme against their own benefactors; and not only do they take away gratitude from among men, but also, lifted up by the boasts of those ignorant of goodness, they suppose they shall escape the evil-hating justice of God, who continually beholds all things. Moreover, often the persuasion of friends entrusted to administer affairs has made many of those appointed to authority partakers of innocent blood and involved them in incurable calamities, as by the false sophistry of malice they have deceived the guileless goodwill of those in authority. And you may observe this not so much from the more ancient histories we have handed down, as by searching out what lies close at hand—things impiously perpetrated through the pestilence of those who wield power unworthily—and take heed for the future, so that we may render the kingdom undisturbed with peace for all men, making use of changes and always judging the matters that come before our eyes with a more equitable response. For indeed, Haman the son of Hammedatha, a Macedonian, in truth a stranger to the blood of the Persians and far removed from our goodness, having been received as a guest by us, obtained such a share of the benevolence we hold toward every nation that he was proclaimed our father and continually remained the second person to the royal throne, receiving obeisance from all; yet, unable to bear his arrogance, he strove to deprive us of both our dominion and our life, and by intricate and deceitful schemes he demanded for destruction both our savior and continual benefactor Mordecai, and Esther, the blameless partner of our kingdom, together with their entire nation. For by these means he thought, having caught us defenseless, to transfer the dominion of the Persians to the Macedonians. But we find that the Jews, who were delivered over to annihilation by that thrice-wicked wretch, are not evildoers, but are governed by the most righteous laws, and are sons of the Most High, the greatest, living God, who directs the kingdom both for us and for our forefathers in the most excellent order. Therefore you will do well not to act upon the letters sent by Haman the son of Hammedatha, because the very man who devised these things has been crucified at the gates of Susa with his entire household, since God, who rules over all things, has swiftly rendered to him the judgment he deserved. Display the copy of this letter openly in every place, and permit the Jews to observe their own laws, and assist them so that they may defend themselves against those who attack them in the time of affliction, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar, on that very day; for God, who has dominion over all things, has made this day a day of gladness for them instead of a day of destruction for the chosen race. Therefore you also, among your named festivals, keep this as a notable day with all feasting, so that both now and afterward it may be deliverance for us and for the well-disposed Persians, but for those who plot against us a memorial of destruction. And every city or province without exception that does not act according to these instructions shall be consumed in wrath with spear and fire; it shall be made not only impassable for men, but also utterly hateful to wild beasts and birds for all time."
verses.8:13: And let the copies be set forth in plain sight throughout the entire kingdom, and let all the Jews be ready for that day to fight against their adversaries.
verses.8:14: So the horsemen went out in haste to carry out the things spoken by the king; and the decree was also posted in Susa.
verses.8:15: Now Mordecai went out arrayed in the royal robe, wearing a golden crown and a diadem of purple fine linen; and when those in Susa saw him, they rejoiced.
verses.8:16: And for the Jews there was light and gladness,
verses.8:17: in every city and province wherever the decree was posted, wherever the proclamation was posted: joy and gladness for the Jews, feasting and gladness. And many of the Gentiles were circumcised and lived as Jews, because of the fear of the Jews.
verses.9:1: For in the twelfth month, on the thirteenth day of the month, which is Adar, the letters written by the king were at hand.
verses.9:2: On that same day those who opposed the Jews perished; for no one withstood them, fearing them.
verses.9:3: For the rulers of the satraps and the governors and the royal scribes honored the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai lay upon them.
verses.9:4: For the king's decree had arrived to be proclaimed throughout all the kingdom.
verses.9:6: And in the city itself the Jews slew five hundred men,
verses.9:10: the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha the Bugaean, the enemy of the Jews; and they took plunder
verses.9:11: on that same day. And the number of those who had perished in Susa was reported to the king.
verses.9:12: Then the king said to Esther, "The Jews have destroyed five hundred men in the city of Susa; and in the surrounding region, how do you suppose they have acted? What more, then, do you request, and it shall be yours?"
verses.9:13: And Esther said to the king, "Let it be granted to the Jews to act in the same manner tomorrow, so as to hang the ten sons of Haman."
verses.9:14: And he permitted it to be done so, and he gave over to the Jews of the city the bodies of the sons of Haman to hang.
verses.9:15: And the Jews in Susa assembled on the fourteenth day of Adar and slew three hundred men, and they plundered nothing.
verses.9:16: Now the rest of the Jews who were in the kingdom assembled and defended themselves, and had rest from their enemies; for they destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth day of Adar, and they plundered nothing.
verses.9:17: And they rested on the fourteenth day of that same month, and kept it as a day of rest with joy and gladness.
verses.9:18: But the Jews who were in the city of Susa assembled also on the fourteenth day and did not rest; and they also kept the fifteenth day with joy and gladness.
verses.9:19: Therefore, the Jews who are scattered throughout every outlying region keep the fourteenth day of Adar as a good day with gladness, each sending portions to his neighbor. And those who dwell in the chief cities keep also the fifteenth day of Adar as a good day of gladness, sending out portions to their neighbors as well.
verses.9:20: And Mordecai wrote these words in a book, and sent them out to all the Jews who were in the kingdom of Artaxerxes, to those near and those far off,
verses.9:21: to establish these good days, and to keep the fourteenth and the fifteenth days of Adar;
verses.9:22: for in these days the Jews had rest from their enemies; and as for the month in which it was turned for them, which was Adar, from mourning into joy and from sorrow into a good day, they were to keep the whole of it as good days of feasting and gladness, sending out portions to their friends and to the poor.
verses.9:23: And the Jews accepted what Mordecai had written to them,
verses.9:24: how Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Macedonian, waged war against them, as he set a decree and a lot to annihilate them,
verses.9:25: and how he went in to the king, speaking to hang Mordecai; yet all the evil things he undertook to bring upon the Jews came upon himself, and he was hanged, both he and his children.
verses.9:26: Therefore these days were called Phrourai, on account of the lots, because in their language they are called Phrourai; on account of the words of this letter, and all that they had suffered on account of these things, and all that had happened to them,
verses.9:27: and he established it. And the Jews took it upon themselves, and upon their seed, and upon those joined to them, nor indeed shall they ever act otherwise. And these days are a memorial celebrated generation after generation, in every city, family, and province.
verses.9:28: And these days of Phrourai shall be observed for all time, and their memorial shall by no means fail from the generations.
verses.9:29: And Queen Esther, the daughter of Aminadab, and Mordecai the Jew wrote all that they had done, and the confirmation of the letter of Phrourai.
verses.9:31: And Mordecai and Queen Esther established it for themselves upon themselves, establishing at that time their counsel also upon their own well-being.
verses.9:32: And Esther established it by word forever, and it was written for a memorial.
verses.10:1: Now the king wrote upon the kingdom of the land and of the sea.
verses.10:2: And his might and valor, and the wealth and glory of his kingdom—behold, they are written in the book of the kings of the Persians and Medes for a memorial.
verses.10:3: Now Mordecai was deputy to King Artaxerxes, and he was great in the kingdom and honored by the Jews; and being beloved, he set forth the way of life to all his nation. And Mordecai said, "From God these things have come to pass. For I remembered the dream which I saw concerning these matters, for not even a word of them has passed away: the little spring that became a river, and there was light and the sun and much water. Esther is the river, whom the king married and made queen; and the two dragons are I and Haman; and the nations are those gathered together to destroy the name of the Jews; and my nation, this is Israel, those who cried out to God and were saved. And the Lord saved His people, and the Lord delivered us from all these evils; and God performed the great signs and wonders which have not come to pass among the nations. Therefore He made two lots, one for the people of God and one for all the nations; and these two lots came to the hour and the appointed time and to the day of judgment before God and for all the nations, and God remembered His people, and He vindicated His own inheritance. And these days shall be for them in the month of Adar, on the fourteenth and the fifteenth of the same month, with assembly and joy and gladness before God, from generation to generation forever among His people Israel." In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemy and Cleopatra, Dositheus, who said that he was a priest and a Levite, and Ptolemy his son brought in the foregoing letter of Phrourai, which they declared to be genuine and to have been translated by Lysimachus the son of Ptolemy, one of those in Jerusalem.

notes.1:1: The Septuagint opens with the Greek prologue (Addition A) recounting Mordecai's dream and the conspiracy of the eunuchs Gabatha and Tharra; it also identifies the Persian king as Artaxerxes (Hebrew: Ahasuerus) and calls Haman a "Bougaean" (Hebrew: Agagite).
notes.1:5: The Septuagint reads "the days of the marriage feast" and specifies "six days," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "these days" and "seven days."
notes.1:9: The Septuagint renders the queen's name as Astin (Hebrew: Vashti), and likewise gives distinct Greek forms for the names of the seven eunuchs (1:10), the three counselors (1:14), Muchaeus (1:16), and Gai (2:8).
notes.2:7: The Septuagint names Esther's father as Amminadab (Hebrew: Abihail) and states that Mordecai brought her up "for himself as a wife," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "as his own daughter."
notes.2:16: The Septuagint places Esther's entry before the king in the twelfth month, Adar, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads the tenth month, Tebeth.
notes.2:20: The Septuagint adds Mordecai's charge to Esther "to fear God and to keep His commandments," underscoring her continued religious faithfulness in the royal court.
notes.3:7: The Septuagint specifies that the lot fell on the fourteenth day of Adar (compare 3:13), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text names only the month here and assigns the thirteenth day of Adar in 3:13.
notes.3:13: This verse includes the full text of King Artaxerxes' decree (Addition B), written in formal Hellenistic royal chancery style and absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:5: "Achrathaeus" preserves the Septuagint name (Ἁχραθαῖος), corresponding to "Hathach" in the Hebrew text; verse 4:6 is absent in the Septuagint.
notes.4:8: The Greek shifts directly from indirect instructions into Mordecai's direct appeal to Esther and explicitly includes the command to "call upon the Lord," which is absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.4:17: In the Septuagint, verse 4:17 incorporates Addition C, containing the prayers of Mordecai and Esther; the critical Greek text reads simply "they have set their hands" without mentioning the hands of idols.
notes.5:1: Verses 5:1–2 incorporate Septuagint Addition D, expanding Esther's audience before the king; the phrase "a general one" (κοινόν) means the royal ordinance applies to ordinary subjects rather than to the queen.
notes.5:8: The Septuagint reads "tomorrow I will do the same," differing from the Hebrew text, which has Esther promise to do as the king has said.
notes.5:10: "Zosara" preserves the Septuagint name (Ζωσάρα) for Haman's wife, corresponding to "Zeresh" in the Hebrew text.
notes.6:1: The Septuagint explicitly attributes the king's sleeplessness to "the Lord" and refers to the court reader as his "tutor" (διδάσκαλος).
notes.6:2: "Artaxerxes" preserves the Septuagint name of the Persian king (Ἀρταξέρξης), corresponding to "Ahasuerus" in the Hebrew text.
notes.6:13: The Septuagint explicitly adds "because the living God is with him," an affirmation absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.7:3: The Greek text reads logos ("word" or "matter"), where some manuscripts and the Hebrew read "my people" (laos).
notes.7:4: Greek diabolos ("slanderer" or "accuser") is applied to Haman here and in 8:1.
notes.7:9: "Bugathan" is the Septuagint name corresponding to Harbonah in the Hebrew text; the Greek verb stauroo ("crucify" or "impale") is used here and in 8:12 for execution on the fifty-cubit xylon ("gallows" or "timber").
notes.8:1: Throughout Greek Esther the king is named "Artaxerxes" rather than Ahasuerus.
notes.8:9: The Septuagint dates the royal summons to the first month, "Nisa" (Nisan), rather than the third month, Sivan, as in the Hebrew text.
notes.8:12: This verse contains the Greek royal decree known as Addition E, which identifies Haman as a Macedonian rather than an Agagite and explicitly attributes the Jews' deliverance to the living God.
notes.8:17: The Septuagint explicitly adds that many Gentiles "were circumcised" as well as living as Jews (ioudaizon).
notes.9:4: The Greek wording here diverges from the Hebrew (which speaks of Mordecai's growing fame), and verse 9:5 is absent from the Septuagint.
notes.9:7: By dividing the first name into "Pharsan" and "Nestain," the Septuagint lists eleven names in 9:7-9 before calling them "the ten sons of Haman" in 9:10; in 9:10 Haman is also called "the Bugaean" (Hebrew Agagite) and the Greek omits the negative before "they took plunder."
notes.9:16: The Septuagint records "fifteen thousand" slain in the provinces, compared with seventy-five thousand in the Hebrew text.
notes.9:26: "Phrourai" is the Septuagint Greek form corresponding to Purim; in 9:29 Esther's father is likewise given the Septuagint name "Aminadab" (Hebrew Abihail).
notes.9:31: Verse 9:30 is absent from the Greek text, and the syntax of 9:31—literally establishing their counsel "upon [or against] their own well-being"—is difficult and differs notably from the Hebrew.
notes.10:1: The Septuagint reads literally "wrote upon" without a direct object; some Greek manuscripts add "taxes," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "laid a tribute."
notes.10:2: The Greek text lists the "Persians and Medes" in this order, reversing the order "Medes and Persians" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.10:3: As throughout Greek Esther, the king is named Artaxerxes (Hebrew: Ahasuerus). This verse includes the Septuagint conclusion (Addition F), presenting Mordecai's interpretation of his dream and the translator's colophon naming the festival "Phrourai" (the Greek form of Purim).
